## Post Office Bay on Floreana: how the Galápagos mail barrel works

**Post Office Bay (Bahía del Correo) is a historic stop on Floreana Island in the Galápagos archipelago.** A wooden mail barrel stands here, and travelers use it according to a tradition dating back to whaling ships: some leave letters, while others collect those they can deliver on their way home.

On a trip around the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), this is an unusual place: the focus shifts from wildlife and volcanoes to the people who crossed the Pacific Ocean. Unlike an ordinary museum, the tradition lets visitors take part in the story, although neither delivery nor a delivery date is guaranteed.

## How mail reached an uninhabited shore

In **1793**, sailors calling at Floreana began using a wooden barrel for letters. Whaling vessels spent many months at sea, and the islands had no regular postal service. Captains and crew left addressed messages hoping that another ship heading toward the appropriate port could deliver them upon arrival.

The barrel's history is described by Galápagos Conservancy and Ecuadorian national park materials. The key idea is simple: messages traveled through people's movements and their willingness to help one another, without flight schedules or a postal company.

There is no operating government post office on this shore today. **Post Office Bay is a historic place name and a voluntary custom** maintained by visitors. Bringing a postcard makes sense for the experience, not as a reliable urgent delivery method.

## How to send a postcard through the barrel

The usual procedure is straightforward: write a postcard, add the recipient's full address, and put it in the barrel. Then look through the messages left behind to see whether any are addressed to a city or country you will soon return to. If so, you can take one for personal delivery later.

This is an exchange based on trust, not a postal-service contract. A postcard may arrive surprisingly quickly, take a long time, or never reach its recipient. Avoid including confidential information, valuables, or documents. A short greeting and a normal postal address that you are comfortable sharing with participants in this tradition are enough.

Access to the barrel, permitted landings, and allowed activities on shore are determined by protected-area authorities and the accompanying guide. Respect the objects already there, do not add your own inscriptions, and take any packaging or rubbish away with you.

## Where Post Office Bay is and how to visit it

The bay lies on [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) in the southern Galápagos. It is a separate island, not part of [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) on Santa Cruz. Visits are normally part of a boat itinerary with a landing at an authorized site. You cannot drive independently here from another island.

Depending on the program, Floreana itineraries may include several distinct stops: [Punta Cormorant](/ecuador/place/punta-cormorant/) with its lagoon and birds, [Devil's Crown](/ecuador/place/devils-crown/) for snorkeling, and [Baroness Lookout](/ecuador/place/baroness-lookout/). They provide different experiences: human history, wildlife observation, and water activities. Not every cruise visits all of them simply because Floreana is on the itinerary.

At Post Office Bay itself, you can also see the volcanic shore and small bay. An unhurried introduction to the site's history is enough for a memorable visit. Strenuous sport is not the main purpose of landing here.

## Post Office Bay on Ada Tours itineraries

On our [8-day VIP yacht cruise around the Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), Post Office Bay features on **day two on Floreana**. After Punta Cormorant and the marine activities, you visit the mail barrel and then continue toward Mirador de la Baronesa. This is an established stop within a broader day's program, rather than a separate lengthy excursion.

Our [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos tour with a cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) also includes Floreana and Post Office Bay, but the trip as a whole is very different: it covers mainland Ecuador and a separate marine stage. Compare the actual number of days spent in the archipelago and the landings included.

For additional islands, browse our [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/). Cruise availability and itineraries depend on the current offerings, so check that your selected trip specifically visits the bay.

## How Post Office Bay differs from other Galápagos stops

| Place | Main reason to visit |
|---|---|
| Post Office Bay | Maritime history and the mail barrel |
| [Punta Cormorant](/ecuador/place/punta-cormorant/) | Lagoon and coastal birds |
| [Puerto Egas](/ecuador/place/puerto-egas/) | Lava coast and fur seals |

Puerto Egas is on Santiago Island. Even when both sites feature on one cruise, they are visited at different stages of the voyage, with a sea crossing between the islands. Post Office Bay is particularly memorable because you can leave a personal message on a distant Pacific shore.

## Frequently asked questions about Post Office Bay

### Is the mail barrel still used?

Yes. Visitors continue to leave and collect postcards. This is a voluntary tradition without guaranteed delivery dates.

### When did the postal tradition begin?

Historical accounts trace the barrel to **1793** and whaling vessels calling at Floreana.

### Can you visit the bay without a cruise?

The bay is on a separate island and requires an appropriate marine itinerary and an authorized landing. Check the actual options in the current program rather than relying on the island's name alone.

### Do Ada Tours itineraries include Post Office Bay?

Yes. For example, our [8-day Galápagos yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) includes the mail-barrel visit on its Floreana day.

## Tours to Post Office Bay: Floreana's history on a cruise

[Post Office Bay](/ecuador/place/post-office-bay/) lies on [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) in the Galápagos archipelago. Its principal attraction is the mail barrel recalling the days of whaling ships. Letters were left here as early as 1793; sailors collected mail addressed to places on their route and delivered it along the way. This tradition survives as an exchange of postcards among travelers.

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Post Office Bay on their main itinerary. Both include a marine voyage and a visit to Floreana, but their overall formats differ: one concentrates entirely on the Galápagos, while the other first explores mainland Ecuador and the Amazon.

## The 8-day Aqua Mare cruise

The [8-day VIP Galápagos yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) begins on [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). **On day two**, the yacht calls at Floreana. The program includes Post Office Bay and other natural attractions on the island.

That same day includes [Punta Cormorant](/ecuador/place/punta-cormorant/) and [Devil's Crown](/ecuador/place/devils-crown/). At Punta Cormorant, the coastal scenery and lagoon birds are highlights; at Devil's Crown, attention turns to volcanic formations and marine life. One island day thus brings together maritime history, shore walks, and wildlife observation.

This cruise is worth considering when the Galápagos archipelago is the main focus of your trip. Post Office Bay remains a short themed stop, not a separate multi-day destination. Exact landing arrangements and the sequence of stops depend on the approved cruise itinerary.

## Eighteen days: Floreana after the Andes and Amazon

On our [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos cruise tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), the Galápagos form the end of a journey beginning in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) and including an Amazonian program around [Pilchicocha Lake](/ecuador/place/pilchicocha-lake/). After the mountains and forests, travelers embark on a 4-day voyage aboard M/Y Grand Majestic.

**Day 16** includes a visit to Post Office Bay, combined with Punta Cormorant and Devil's Crown. Walking and water-based activities have different conditions, so establish in advance where visitors will land and where they will observe marine wildlife from the water.

This option appeals to travelers drawn to the contrast between mainland nature and the Galápagos. A lake amid Amazonian forest, highland landscapes, and island coasts provide three very different experiences, but require more time, changes of transportation, and thoughtful packing.

## What happens at the famous mail barrel?

At the old barrel, visitors can leave a postcard without using the normal postal system and check whether any messages could genuinely be delivered by hand after returning home. The tradition is based on person-to-person delivery. It differs from a conventional post office: the barrel provides no delivery guarantee and does not replace official mail services.

The bay's history complements the natural attractions of the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). It draws attention to people who crossed the Pacific long before modern tourism infrastructure existed. For a personal souvenir, bring an addressed postcard and allow only the time allocated by the guide for this stop.

## Planning a landing on Floreana

Access to Galápagos visitor sites is governed by protected-area rules. On a cruise, the authorized ship route, sea conditions, landing time, and instructions of accompanying guides matter. Swell may require changes to the order of stops. Confirm the scheduled time at the barrel from the final itinerary rather than transferring the timetable from another cruise.

On Floreana, Post Office Bay can be compared with marine experiences at Devil's Crown and nature walks at Punta Cormorant. They are separate attractions, so check for each one rather than simply looking for the word "Floreana" on a list of islands.

We can help compare these two routes by duration, order of island landings, and the mainland stage. For more options, see [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and [cruise expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Post Office Bay

### Can you send a letter through the mail barrel?

You can leave a postcard as part of the local custom, but delivery depends on other travelers. It is a voluntary exchange of correspondence, not an official postal service.

### Which island is the bay on?

Post Office Bay is on Floreana in the Galápagos archipelago. In both itineraries described here, it is a stop during the cruise stage.

### Is the bay included in both tours?

Yes. In both current itineraries, Post Office Bay is part of the main Floreana program. The day differs: day two of the 8-day cruise and day sixteen of the 18-day tour.

### Should you choose a cruise just for the mail barrel?

Probably not: the stop itself is relatively short. Choose a cruise based on the full sequence of islands, landings, and wildlife experiences, treating Post Office Bay as an engaging historical episode.

## Puerto Ayora in the Galápagos: harbor, town, and island excursion base

[Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) is on the southern shore of [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). It is a town where travelers stay between land and sea excursions around the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Hotels, restaurants, a waterfront, and docks offer a place to return after a long excursion day and prepare for the next.

The key planning question is **what you can actually see in town and which attractions require a separate trip**. The harbor and streets can be explored on an ordinary walk. Seeing tortoises in the wild, visiting lava tunnels, or reaching remote marine sites requires separate routes.

## What to see in Puerto Ayora

Start with the waterfront and harbor. Small boats, excursion vessels, and local transport gather at the piers. Sea lions and birds may sometimes be seen by the water. Even in town, a central Galápagos rule applies: do not approach animals to take photos, feed them, or touch them.

Puerto Ayora is home to the **Charles Darwin Research Station**, an active scientific and conservation center. Areas open to visitors explain research work, the history of the islands, and efforts to conserve endemic plants and animals. It is a separate attraction for travelers who are interested in biology as well as scenery.

A well-known nature walk near town is Tortuga Bay. Reaching it takes time on a walking trail and requires compliance with visitor access rules; it should not be treated as a beach stop just outside the hotel. If a full-day boat excursion is already planned, reserve that walk for a free morning or a separate day.

## How Puerto Ayora differs from Santa Cruz Island

| Location | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Puerto Ayora | Harbor, town, research station |
| Highlands | Tortoises, lava tunnels |
| Other islands | Marine wildlife and landings |

The [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) lie inland. They offer opportunities to observe giant tortoises in their natural habitat and learn about volcanic formations. These are distinct from a town walk, so allow for an overland transfer.

There are more options for a quiet evening and rest after travel near town. Inland areas are primarily natural sites. Outlying islands require a boat, an authorized itinerary, and sufficient time at sea.

## Getting here from Baltra Airport

Many visitors arrive from the mainland at [Baltra Island](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/). The onward journey includes the drive to Itabaca Channel, a short crossing to Santa Cruz, and a road transfer south to Puerto Ayora. A hotel in town is therefore not next to the airport.

On our [Ada Tours New Year Ecuador and Galápagos program](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), the group crosses Itabaca after landing on Baltra, visits the Santa Cruz highlands, sees tortoises and lava tunnels, and then continues to the hotel in Puerto Ayora. This sequence leaves the following day free for a marine excursion.

Special entry procedures, conservation fees, and luggage checks apply in the Galápagos. Check the procedures and costs against official information before traveling, as they depend on visitor category and current regulations.

## Marine excursions: where do they start?

Having a harbor in town does not mean **every** excursion yacht departs from central Puerto Ayora. Some routes first require a transfer north to Itabaca Channel before the marine part of the trip begins.

For example, [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) is known for volcanic slopes and the view of Pinnacle Rock. On our [Complete Ecuador New Year tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), the excursion starts with an early transfer to Itabaca, followed by a yacht crossing, a walk to the viewpoint, and time for snorkeling. The group returns to Puerto Ayora.

The next island day on that tour follows a different plan: **one of two alternatives** is offered — North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. It does not involve visiting all four locations on one itinerary. When choosing a tour or booking a separate excursion, confirm which route is arranged, where the boat departs, and what the price includes.

## Spending a free evening

After a day at sea, it is convenient to walk along the waterfront, have dinner, and prepare for the next early start. Staying in town is usually more practical for such evenings than sleeping far from settlements. However, a Puerto Ayora hotel does not automatically shorten every boat excursion: travel to the departure point may take a separate part of the day.

For a boat outing, bring sun and wind protection and waterproof packaging for your phone and belongings. If you are prone to seasickness, discuss precautions with a doctor in advance. It can feel warm ashore but much cooler on a moving yacht. Sea and wind conditions change with the season and the exact date.

## Choosing an itinerary with accommodation in Puerto Ayora

Compare the number of **full days**, specific islands visited, boat departure points, and the details of land-based visits. Not every Galápagos itinerary includes the Darwin Research Station or a special highlands visit; staying in Puerto Ayora does not mean these attractions are included.

On our current [Ada Tours Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), Puerto Ayora is a base for several of the final days. For broader options, see the [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/) and our [Galápagos guide](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

## Frequently asked questions about Puerto Ayora

### Is Puerto Ayora on Baltra?

No. [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) is the airport island, while Puerto Ayora is on the southern shore of Santa Cruz. They are connected by a water crossing and a road transfer.

### Can you see giant tortoises while walking around town?

To see them in their natural environment, plan a visit to the [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/). That is a separate land excursion.

### Can you visit Bartolomé from here in one day?

Yes, some programs include a day excursion with a return to town. Boarding may take place away from Puerto Ayora itself, so confirm the entire journey.

### Can visitors enter the Charles Darwin Research Station?

Yes, the scientific center has educational and exhibition areas accessible to visitors. Check current access rules for individual rooms and conservation areas shortly before your visit.

## Tours through Puerto Ayora: Santa Cruz base or cruise?

[Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) is a port town on the southern shore of [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) in Ecuador. Many [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) itineraries pass through here. Travelers stay in town before day excursions, go out to sea, discover island life, or meet the crew of a cruise vessel.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through Puerto Ayora. **Having the town on an itinerary does not mean the length of stay is the same.** Some trips include nights in hotels on land, others pass through during transfers, and cruise itineraries spend most island time aboard.

Compare our programs to choose the format that suits you.

## Traveling through Baltra Island

On some itineraries, travelers arrive in the Galápagos at [Baltra Island](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) Airport. They then cross Itabaca Channel to Santa Cruz and travel south to Puerto Ayora. The landscape changes along the way: the northern dry volcanic areas give way to greener high ground.

Each program handles this journey differently, with group or private transfers, possible stops, landings, and meetings with a guide. **Arrival time at Baltra and check-in time in Puerto Ayora are two separate events.** Do not schedule an essential independent boat excursion on arrival day before confirming all the connections.

Santa Cruz makes it possible to combine the town with the [island highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/), home to giant tortoises and lava tunnels. The chosen itinerary must identify the specific farm or natural site to be visited.

## Land-based option: New Year in Ecuador and the Galápagos

The [Complete Ecuador New Year tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) lasts 11 days and combines Quito, volcanoes, and mainland highland destinations with a final visit to the Galápagos. **On day eight**, the route runs through Baltra and Santa Cruz to Puerto Ayora. The highlands, giant tortoises, and lava tunnels are included along the way.

Accommodation in Puerto Ayora is at Hotel Fiesta 3*. The town serves as a base for later excursions. Island activities include a boat trip to [Bartolomé Island](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) and designated alternative sea outings. Travelers who prefer returning to a hotel on land each evening can compare this format with a yacht cruise.

This is **a specific New Year departure**, not a continuously available year-round itinerary. The dates and exact included excursions matter when choosing.

## The 8-day cruise: Puerto Ayora before the islands

The [8-day Aqua Mare VIP yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) begins with arrival on Santa Cruz. On the first day, guests reach Puerto Ayora and meet the yacht. The program includes the [Charles Darwin Research Station](/ecuador/place/charles-darwin-research-station/) and time to explore the town.

The cruise then heads toward [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/), [Isabela Island](/ecuador/place/isabela-island/), and other places in the archipelago. This is a fundamentally different way to experience the Galápagos: journeys between islands are part of the sea voyage, with overnight stays aboard the vessel according to the program. The amount of free time in Puerto Ayora is not an appropriate measure of this cruise.

## Longer itineraries visiting Puerto Ayora

On our [18-day Ecuador tour with a Galápagos cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), the island section follows travel through the Andes and the Amazon, including [Pilchicocha Lake](/ecuador/place/pilchicocha-lake/). Puerto Ayora is part of the final island stage. The combination of forest, highland, and marine ecosystems makes this trip attractive.

The [12-day Ecuador and Colombia tour](/multi-country/tour/ecuador-colombia-galapagos-12-days/) brings together Quito and the Galápagos with Medellín, Cartagena, and Bogotá. Puerto Ayora features **on day three**, after arriving at Baltra and crossing Santa Cruz. Further island excursions and travel to Colombia follow. The additional international logistics and shifts in the character of the trip are key considerations.

When comparing these programs, look beyond the total tour length to **the number of actual island days**. An 18-day trip with a substantial mainland segment does not necessarily give you more time in Puerto Ayora than a shorter specialist trip.

## What to do with free time in Puerto Ayora

The town lends itself to waterfront and harbor walks, cafés, shops, and local life. The [Charles Darwin Research Station](/ecuador/place/charles-darwin-research-station/) offers scientific and educational interest, explaining research and nature conservation in the archipelago. It is a separate attraction; merely stopping in town does not guarantee admission to the station.

For people interested in [Galápagos wildlife](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/), excursions beyond the waterfront are important. Compare tours featuring [Bartolomé Island](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/), [Bachas Beaches](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/), and other sites only when they are actually included or offered as an alternative. An "either/or" option means one of the routes, not simultaneous visits to all named islands.

## Choosing a tour with a Puerto Ayora stop

First decide where you want to spend your nights: in a town hotel or aboard a vessel. Then compare actual island days, number of sea excursions, transfers through Baltra, guiding arrangements, and the full geography of each trip. A few hours in town on one itinerary and free evenings on another will offer different experiences.

We can help align island and mainland stages within the chosen program. To explore more options, browse the [Ecuador tours catalog](/ecuador/tour/) or our [Cruises and Expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/) section.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Puerto Ayora

### Do all Galápagos tours include an overnight stay in Puerto Ayora?

No. Puerto Ayora can be a land-based accommodation base, a departure point for sea excursions, or a brief cruise stop. Check overnight arrangements on the particular itinerary.

### How do you reach Puerto Ayora from Baltra Airport?

On the itineraries described here, travelers transfer to Itabaca Channel, cross to Santa Cruz, and continue by road to the southern shore. The total journey depends on the flight schedule and transport arrangements.

### Can you see giant tortoises on the way into town?

Some itineraries include the [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) to observe tortoises. That is a separate part of the program, not an automatic feature of driving across the island.

### How does a cruise differ from a land-based hotel trip?

On a cruise, journeys between islands and overnight accommodation take place aboard the vessel. Land-based trips use Puerto Ayora as a base for separate marine excursions. Compare specific stops and landing durations, not just the accommodation category.

## Puerto Egas in the Galápagos: lava shores, grottoes, and fur seals

**Puerto Egas is a landing site on the western shore of Santiago Island, at James Bay in the Galápagos.** Unlike broad sandy beaches, the main walk here follows an uneven volcanic coast. Lava has formed small pools, ledges, and grottoes where Galápagos fur seals find shelter.

Puerto Egas is excellent for observing coastal animals from a distance that feels close but remains safe. Together with the wider [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), it illustrates why volcanic geology matters so much to marine life: animals use fissures, rock shelves, and shaded spaces.

## Where is Puerto Egas?

The site is on [Santiago Island](/ecuador/place/santiago-island/) near James Bay. Visitors arrive by sea; there is no ordinary road access from another island. Visits require an authorized landing as part of a vessel itinerary and compliance with national park rules.

Dark lava shores, small sandy patches, tidal pools, and waves filling natural depressions create the scenery. Dry rock can lie right next to a pool with crabs and other coastal animals. The meeting of ocean and lava is more compelling here than conventional resort facilities.

## The coastal trail to the fur seal grottoes

One main walking route begins at the shore and leads toward the **Fur Seal Grottoes**, rocky shelters used by fur seals. According to Galápagos Conservancy, these animals prefer rocky coasts with shaded sections, and Puerto Egas' grottoes provide exactly such refuges.

On a walk, fur seals may be seen resting among rocks, moving between ledges, or entering the water. Small coves and tidal pools offer further sights: crabs and seabirds are often visible along the shore. Specific sightings depend on conditions and the animals' natural behavior.

**Galápagos fur seals and sea lions are different animals.** A guide can help distinguish them: fur seals more often use shaded rocky shelters, while sea lions frequently rest on more exposed beaches. Do not approach resting animals or pups, or stand between an animal and the water.

The trail surface may be wet and uneven. Shoes need a secure grip on lava rock, and keeping hands free helps with balance. Tides, swell, and weather may alter the route; visitors must not wander away from the marked path on their own.

## The salt crater: another chapter of Puerto Egas

Besides the coastal trail, Puerto Egas has **an inland route to historic salt workings**. Salt was extracted on the island in the 20th century using a natural crater containing brackish water. Galápagos Conservancy dates mining activity to the 1920s and the 1960s. Puerto Egas takes its name from Héctor Egas, whose company operated on the island during the 1960s.

The trail toward the salt crater is different from the walk to the coastal grottoes. Galápagos Conservancy gives the inland path to the crater as about **3 km** long. Along it, the focus shifts from marine animals to dry island vegetation, traces of human activity, and volcanic terrain.

**Do not assume both routes form one mandatory walk.** Landing time is limited by the vessel schedule, and the choice may depend on the group, weather, and trail access. Compare cruises to establish whether they specify the shore grottoes, the salt crater, or a choice between the two.

## Puerto Egas on Ada Tours itineraries

On our [8-day VIP Galápagos yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), Puerto Egas is scheduled **on day five**, devoted to Santiago Island. Guests land on the coast in the morning. We offer around 2 hours for a walk toward the former salt mine, or an alternative: stay by the shore, visit the fur seal grottoes, or go snorkeling.

This distinction matters: the activities are alternatives, so no one should expect every traveler to visit the salt crater, grottoes, and underwater sites in one morning.

Later the same day, the itinerary includes [Espumilla Beach](/ecuador/place/espumilla-beach/) and other marine stops. Puerto Egas features rocky shores and grottoes, while Espumilla is known for its broad sandy coast and natural nesting areas for sea turtles.

To compare cruise-stage lengths, landings, and accommodation formats, use our [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/). On a customized journey, the exact island sequence matters: Puerto Egas cannot be added as a short car excursion from [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/).

## What to consider when visiting

Much of the experience lies in quiet wildlife observation. Do not touch or feed animals or interfere with their movement. Take photographs without chasing fur seals or trying to enter their shelters. Tides and waves can change access to particular sections of the coast path.

Bring comfortable shoes, sun protection, and water for the landing. Snorkeling has separate rules and restrictions and should only be chosen when the itinerary expressly includes it. The presence of lava pools does not mean visitors may swim in all of them.

## Frequently asked questions about Puerto Egas

### Which island is Puerto Egas on?

On [Santiago Island](/ecuador/place/santiago-island/) at James Bay. Travelers reach it by sea from other islands as part of a suitable itinerary.

### Which animals are most commonly seen here?

Galápagos fur seals resting near the rocky grottoes are the main wildlife attraction of the coastal trail. Other coastal animals may also be seen, but sightings are not guaranteed.

### What is the difference between the shore trail and the path to the salt mine?

The coastal trail leads to fur seal grottoes. The inland path goes to the old salt crater linked with 20th-century mining. The landing program determines which route is taken.

### Is Puerto Egas included in an Ada Tours cruise?

Yes. The [8-day Galápagos cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) includes a stop at Puerto Egas on day five, with several alternative walking options.
